intro: Buying a home in Kentucky requires more than saving for a down payment. Your mortgage interest rate, property taxes, homeowners insurance and ongoing maintenance expenses all influence how much you can comfortably afford.

Our free Kentucky mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment before purchasing a property. Whether you're searching for a home in Louisville, Lexington, Bowling Green, Owensboro or a smaller Kentucky community, compare financing scenarios and establish a realistic homebuying budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Kentucky?

blocks.markdown:
A $205,000 Kentucky home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $983.26.

Kentucky offers housing opportunities across major metropolitan areas, suburban communities, agricultural regions and Appalachian towns.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Kentucky housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/KY/HSG010223), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $205,600 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,433, while approximately 68.3% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical statistics provide a useful affordability benchmark but do not represent current home sale prices.

Properties near employment centers in Louisville and Lexington may have different purchase prices from homes in eastern or western Kentucky.

Research comparable property sales in your preferred neighborhood and consider transportation, utilities and maintenance when establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Kentucky Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of the property and your available down payment. The calculator determines the amount you need to borrow before calculating principal and interest.

Choose your preferred repayment term and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

Include the property's annual tax liability, homeowners insurance premium and monthly association fees where applicable.

If your conventional financing requires private mortgage insurance, enter that expense as well.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and experiment with different purchase prices, interest rates and down payments.

Use the amortization schedule to understand how your outstanding mortgage balance changes throughout the repayment period.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing options outside Kentucky.

sections.heading: How Kentucky Property Taxes Affect Mortgage Payments

blocks.markdown:
Kentucky calculates real estate taxes using assessed property values and applicable state and local tax rates.

According to the [Kentucky Department of Revenue's residential property assessment guidance](https://revenue.ky.gov/Property/Residential-Farm-Commercial-Property/Pages/default.aspx), locally elected property valuation administrators, commonly called PVAs, assess real estate at its estimated fair cash value.

For ordinary residential property, this generally reflects the price the property could obtain through a fair voluntary sale.

Your final property tax bill may include state, county, city, school district and other applicable local taxes.

### Kentucky property tax calculation example

Suppose your property has an assessed value of $205,000 and is subject to an illustrative combined property tax rate of $0.90 per $100 of assessed value.

This example assumes no exemptions or additional assessments.

The actual rate depends on the property's location. Consult the [Kentucky Department of Revenue's property tax rate resources](https://revenue.ky.gov/Property/Pages/PropertyTaxRates.aspx) and your local PVA for accurate information.

### Kentucky homestead exemption

Kentucky provides a property tax exemption for qualifying older homeowners and individuals with eligible disabilities.

For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, the exemption is $49,100.

A qualifying property assessed at $205,000 could therefore have its taxable assessed value reduced to $155,900 before applicable tax rates are applied.

This is not a universal exemption available to every homeowner.

Eligibility generally includes being at least 65 years old or meeting qualifying disability requirements, together with ownership and occupancy conditions.

Review the [Kentucky homestead exemption requirements](https://revenue.ky.gov/Property/Residential-Farm-Commercial-Property/Pages/Homestead-Exemption.aspx) and contact your local PVA before incorporating the exemption into your estimate.

Kentucky homeowners face different environmental risks depending on their property's location, construction and condition.

Thunderstorms, tornadoes, flooding and winter weather can affect insurance premiums and maintenance expenses.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before finalizing your purchase.

### Flood insurance

Homes near rivers, streams and low-lying areas may face significant flood exposure.

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding, meaning a separate flood insurance policy may be necessary.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate the property's flood designation.

Include any applicable flood insurance premiums in your estimated monthly housing expenses.

### Mine subsidence insurance

Historical underground mining is an additional consideration for homebuyers in parts of Kentucky.

Mine subsidence occurs when an underground coal mine collapses and causes damage to structures above it.

The [Kentucky Department of Insurance's Mine Subsidence Fund](https://insurance.ky.gov/PPC/newstatic_info.aspx?Static_ID=23\&divid=15) makes specialized coverage available to eligible property owners in 37 counties.

Standard homeowners policies generally exclude this type of damage.

Buyers considering properties in affected counties, including areas of eastern and western Kentucky, should investigate historical mining activity and discuss coverage with their insurance agents.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, insurance, mortgage insurance and association fees.

Use the complete calculator to compare the actual monthly housing expenses associated with individual properties.

The Kentucky Housing Corporation, commonly called KHC, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### Kentucky down payment assistance

The [KHC Down Payment Assistance program](https://kyhousing.org/page/down-payment-assistance) currently offers eligible borrowers assistance of up to $12,500 toward qualifying down payment and closing expenses.

The assistance is structured as a secondary loan with a 15-year repayment period.

KHC's published [mortgage program guidance](https://www.kyhousing.org/page/mortgage-faqs) identifies a fixed interest rate of 4.75% for this assistance arrangement.

Borrowers must account for the second mortgage payment when evaluating affordability.

Because program terms can change, confirm the available assistance amount and interest rate with an approved lender.

### Shared Appreciation Mortgage program

In July 2026, Kentucky Housing Corporation introduced its Shared Appreciation Mortgage program.

The [KHC Shared Appreciation Mortgage](https://www.kyhousing.org/programs/shared-appreciation-mortgage) provides qualifying first-time buyers with financing of up to 25% of an eligible home's purchase price or appraised value.

The program currently focuses on newly constructed homes.

The secondary loan carries no interest or scheduled monthly payments. Instead, borrowers repay the original assistance and an agreed share of property appreciation when qualifying repayment events occur.

These events can include selling the home or paying off the primary mortgage.

Although the arrangement can reduce immediate mortgage expenses, it also creates a future financial obligation. Compare its long-term costs with ordinary mortgage assistance before participating.

Conventional mortgages offer several financing arrangements for eligible borrowers.

FHA-insured mortgages may provide an alternative for households with limited down payment savings.

Eligible veterans, service members and surviving spouses can investigate [VA home loan benefits](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/).

Buyers considering smaller Kentucky communities may also qualify for [USDA Rural Development housing programs](https://www.rd.usda.gov/), depending on household income and property location.

Government-backed mortgage programs have different insurance and funding fee requirements. Obtain a complete lender estimate rather than applying conventional PMI assumptions to every financing arrangement.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Kentucky Home

blocks.markdown:
Kentucky homebuyers should consider expenses that are not automatically included in a standard mortgage payment.

Older properties may require roofing repairs, heating system improvements or electrical upgrades. Rural homes may have private wells, septic systems or access roads requiring maintenance.

Properties on steep or uneven land can also involve drainage and foundation considerations.

Request a professional home inspection and investigate foreseeable maintenance expenses before purchasing.

Buyers moving between rural communities and major employment centers should account for commuting costs. A lower purchase price may not fully compensate for substantially higher transportation expenses.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Kentucky?

blocks.markdown:
Start with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract household expenses, debt payments and savings contributions.

Use our [Kentucky Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/kentucky-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to assess your borrowing obligations.

Maintain enough savings to cover closing costs, emergency repairs and insurance deductibles.

Compare several mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Remember that the maximum amount a lender approves may exceed the amount that comfortably fits your household budget.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $205,000 Kentucky home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year loan term, principal and interest would be approximately $983.26 per month. Taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### Who qualifies for Kentucky's homestead exemption?

Homeowners aged 65 or older and individuals meeting applicable disability requirements may qualify. Ownership and occupancy conditions also apply. The exemption amount for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100.

### Does Kentucky offer down payment assistance for first-time buyers?

Yes. Kentucky Housing Corporation offers qualifying borrowers down payment assistance and other financing options, including its new Shared Appreciation Mortgage program. Eligibility, property requirements and repayment conditions vary.

Use our Kentucky mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments and repayment terms before committing to a property.

Replace illustrative taxes and insurance premiums with verified property-specific estimates. Understanding your complete monthly housing expenses can help you select a home that supports sustainable homeownership.
